'''Raphaël Granier de Cassagnac''' (born 1 January 1973 in Paris) is a French [[physicist]] and writer.

== Career ==
=== Research ===
He is specialized in nuclear and particle physics. He is a member of the [[PHENIX]]&nbsp;experiment at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]&nbsp;and of the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]]&nbsp;experiment at [[CERN]] where he is involved in studying the [[Quark-Gluon Plasma]] in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions.

=== Writing ===
He writes science fiction novels. His debut novel was ''Eternity Incorporated'', published in 2011. It was followed by ''Thinking Eternity'' in 2014 which won the Prix du Lundi in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.quarante-deux.org/prix/Prix_du_Lundi/|title=Prix du Lundi : lauréats - Quarante-Deux/un Honneur insoutenable|website=quarante-deux.org}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Ahead of the [[2024 French legislative election]], he co-signed a statement with other figures from French [[speculative fiction]] in support of a [[New Popular Front]] against the far-right.<ref>{{cite web|date=13 June 2024|title=Actrices et acteurs des littératures de l'imaginaire pour le Front populaire|url=https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/legislatives-2024/actrices-et-acteurs-des-litteratures-de-limaginaire-pour-le-front-populaire|author-last=|author-first=|access-date=23 June 2024|work=L'Humanité}}</ref>
